claims.subject: rsp-v3-1
claims.statement: Anthropic’s Responsible Scaling Policy v3.1 keeps the footnote saying that where laws such as California SB 53 define “catastrophic risk” or similar terms with specific thresholds, Anthropic addresses those requirements in separate compliance frameworks.
claims.qualification: The edition names SB 53 and points to separate compliance frameworks; it does not say that the RSP is a framework under the Act. Not evidence of compliance. The dataset’s v3.0 record (sb-link-rsp-v3-0) cites the same footnote in v3.4 as further evidence; this record gives each later edition its own link, as the dataset does for the White House and Seoul links.

evidence.passage: Where laws such as California SB 53 define this or similar terms with specific thresholds, we address those requirements in separate compliance frameworks.

claims.subject: preparedness-beta-2023
claims.statement: OpenAI’s Preparedness Framework (Beta) describes the framework as one more way in which OpenAI is meeting the voluntary commitments on safety, security and trust in AI that it made in July 2023.

time.note: The edition’s publication date as recorded in the dataset.

claims.qualification: The framework’s own statement that it is a way of meeting the commitments. The text does not name the White House or a specific commitment; the July 2023 date and wording match the July 2023 commitments text, to which OpenAI is listed as a party (cm-wh-2023-07-openai). Not evidence that any commitment was met.

evidence.passage: This is also one more way in which we are meeting our voluntary commitments to safety, security and trust in AI that we made in July 2023.
evidence.note: Identification of the commitments text rests on the date and the three named aims (safety, security, trust), which are the July 2023 text’s headings; flagged for checking.

claims.subject: frontier-governance-2026
claims.statement: OpenAI’s Frontier Governance Framework (May 2026 edition) states that it covers frontier models as defined under California’s TFAIA and general-purpose models with systemic risk under the EU AI Act.

time.note: Publication date established by the release announcement, as recorded in the dataset.

claims.qualification: The framework names the AI Act to set its own scope. Whether any OpenAI model is a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk is legal application and is not recorded. Not evidence of compliance. The copy checked carries no edition date and may be a later expression of the May 2026 edition (see the framework comparison pack).

evidence.locator: Section 1 “Introduction”, scope paragraph, PDF p. 4 (printed p. 2)
evidence.passage: Paraphrase: the FGF says it covers frontier models as the TFAIA defines them and general-purpose models with systemic risk under the EU AI Act, and that by systemic risks it means both the TFAIA’s catastrophic risks and the AI Act’s systemic risks.
evidence.note: Paraphrased because the edition’s quotation budget in the dataset is nearly spent (389 of 400 words).

evidence.passage: Paraphrase: the sentence on the EU Code of Practice (already quoted in cm-link-frontier-governance-2026-eu-code) ends by naming the models covered under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, the EU AI Act.

claims.subject: frontier-governance-2026
claims.statement: OpenAI’s Frontier Governance Framework (May 2026 edition) lists, among the cases in which it will not consider an update of a Model Report necessary, a model considered similarly safe or safer “under Appendix 2.2 of the Code of Practice”.
claims.qualification: A provision-level reference to the Code in the framework’s own words. It records what the framework says it will use, not how Appendix 2.2 was applied to any model and not compliance. Proposed as a second evidence item for the existing link record cm-link-frontier-governance-2026-eu-code, or as its own record (open question). The copy checked carries no edition date.

evidence.locator: Section 4 “Model reporting”, “Model report updates”, PDF p. 18 (printed p. 16)
evidence.passage: under Appendix 2.2 of the Code of Practice
evidence.note: The surrounding sentence lists three cases in which no Model Report update may be needed: (1) capabilities not materially changed, (2) a more capable model planned within a month, (3) a model considered similarly safe or safer, with the quoted reference. Short quote because the edition’s budget in the dataset is nearly spent.

claims.subject: ms-fgf-2026
claims.statement: Microsoft’s Frontier Governance Framework (February 2026) runs a leading indicator assessment on any model in scope for frontier model requirements under applicable laws, naming the EU AI Act among them.

time.note: Month on the cover; a publication day is not established.

claims.qualification: The framework names the AI Act to set when an assessment runs. Which Microsoft models are in scope of the Act is legal application and is not recorded. Not evidence of compliance. The same sentence is cited for SB 53 in sb-link-ms-fgf-2026.

commitment.scope: trigger for the leading indicator assessment

evidence.locator: Section 3 “Evaluation and assessment”, “Monitoring for leading indicators of tracked high-risk capabilities”, PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5)
evidence.passage: A leading indicator assessment is run on any model that is in scope for frontier model requirements under applicable laws, such as the EU AI Act
evidence.note: Overlaps the passage already quoted for sb-link-ms-fgf-2026; counted once.

claims.subject: ms-fgf-2026
claims.statement: Microsoft’s Frontier Governance Framework (February 2026) names New York’s RAISE Act among the laws whose frontier model requirements trigger its leading indicator assessment, and its change log describes the edition as a one-year update following finalisation of the RAISE Act, among other texts.

time.note: Month on the cover; a publication day is not established. The edition predates Chapter 96 of 2026 (signed 27 March 2026), so it refers to the Act as signed in December 2025.

claims.qualification: The framework’s own statements. The change log states a sequence, not a reason the Act required; no causal claim is recorded. Not evidence of compliance. The object is the RAISE Act as described by the Governor (new-york-raise-act), not Chapter 96.

evidence.locator: Section 3 “Evaluation and assessment”, PDF p. 6 (printed p. 5)
evidence.passage: New York’s Responsible AI Safety and Education (RAISE) Act
evidence.note: Continues the sentence quoted in fl-link-ms-fgf-2026-eu-ai-act.

evidence.locator: Appendix II “Change log”, February 2026 entry, PDF p. 16 (printed p. 15)
evidence.passage: One year update following finalization of the EU Code of Practice for General Purpose AI (CoP), NY RAISE Act and CA Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act
evidence.note: Already quoted in the dataset for cm-link-ms-fgf-2026-eu-code and sb-link-ms-fgf-2026; counted once.

omissions.item: Google DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework v3.1, footnote 1
omissions.reason: It cites Anthropic’s SB 53 compliance-framework announcement and a GOV.UK publication as examples of industry practice; it does not name SB 53 or any commitment itself. A citation of a document about a law is not a link to the law.

omissions.item: Statements that a framework references voluntary technical standards (NIST AI Risk Management Framework, NIST SP 800-53, ISO/IEC 42001, SOC 2, FedRAMP) in xAI FAIF 2025, Microsoft FGF 2025, OpenAI Preparedness v2 and OpenAI FGF 2026
omissions.reason: Voluntary technical standards are outside this pack’s instruments (commitments, codes and laws).

omissions.item: Generic references to “regulatory requirements”, “applicable laws” or “regulators” without naming an instrument (RSP v2.0–v3.4, Meta AASF v2.0, Microsoft FGF 2026, OpenAI FGF 2026)
omissions.reason: No instrument is named; a link is recorded only where the document names the text.

omissions.item: OpenAI FGF 2026, Section 6: OpenAI Ireland Limited as provider of OpenAI’s GPAI-SR models and responsible for compliance with the EU Code; OpenAI OpCo LLC responsible for compliance with the TFAIA
omissions.reason: Set aside in week 4c as legal application (docs/control-commitments.md); not re-opened here.

openQuestions.question: Should a provision-level reference such as OpenAI FGF’s “under Appendix 2.2 of the Code of Practice” be a second evidence item on the existing link record or its own record?
openQuestions.recommended: A second evidence item on cm-link-frontier-governance-2026-eu-code: one link per edition and instrument, with each passage that makes the link.
